description:
FILED s476 (Fable, 2026-09-07) -- USER ask: "Please make a note of adding method calls to the speed table, so it is kept visible. (No hurry, next time.)"

WHAT: the README speed table (README.md, the 19-row `benchmark | what it measures | PCL / perl` table, = the 2026-09-07 quiet-box board of docs/faster-codegen-suggestions.md §0.2k) has NO method-call row, although the bench (tools/bench-exec.pl) has two and the §0.2k board measured both:
  methret   plain method call `$o->bump` on a blessed hash, 1M calls   PCL/perl 1.51x  (0.0883 s perl, 0.1336 s PCL)
  moo-objs  a Moo class: constructor, rw/ro accessors, a method building another object, 20k iterations   29.45x  (0.0395 s perl, 1.1629 s PCL)
  (subret, the plain-sub twin, reads 0.41x -- the contrast methret exists for.)

DO, at the NEXT README speed-table refresh (a quiet-box board re-measure, never a derived ratio -- the s475 rule): add `methret` ("a method call on a blessed hash, `$o->bump`") and `moo-objs` ("Moo objects: constructor, accessors, a method building an object") as rows, in the table’s sorted position, so method-call speed stays VISIBLE on the front page; re-read the prose around the table against the new rows (the "fourteen of nineteen rows beat perl" sentence changes to the new counts).  Keep the §0.2k board as the source: a README number is a measured board number.

NOT: no bench change, no new row -- both rows exist; this is a visibility edit.  Owner: whoever runs the next quiet-box board (Fable, the "owed once quiet" list) -- ride it in that commit.

=== DONE (s479, Fable, 2026-09-08) ===
README speed table refreshed from the s479 quiet-box board (docs/faster-codegen-suggestions.md section 0.2m, main a9f2a264, gen v2-1080, load 0.86-1.20): 23 rows, `methret` (1.06x) and `moo-objs` (32.3x) added in sorted position, every ratio refreshed, the slice sentence and the overload paragraph re-read against the rows (method calls are now level with perl; the Moo row is compile-load dominated, #1189).  Three wrong-way movers vs the s475 board (arrhash-k, regexg, moo-objs) were run down before the table was written: runtime A/B + macroexpansion + a PADDING-ONLY runtime probe show CODE PLACEMENT (10-12 % from an unused defun) and load, not a cost -- DECIDED s479, the placement rule.  Raw runs: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s479/.
